Definition: (figuratively) to love; by implication, a love-token, lover, friend; specifically an uncle
KeyPassages: Song of Solomon 1:2; Song of Solomon 1:4; Song of Solomon 4:10; Song of Solomon 7:12
BiblicalUsage: Beloved, the word for the lover in the Song, whose love is better than wine, and whose name the bride calls out again and again. The beloved's love is sweeter than wine and more fragrant than ointments, and the bride begs him to come away to the fields. The same word names the uncle and the kinsman elsewhere, but here it is love speaking.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Song gives me a word for Christ that no other book does: He is my beloved, and His love is better than wine. The love that draws the bride to the fields is the same love that drew Christ to the cross, and I answer it by going where He calls.
